section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Bloom's Taxonomy — Three Domains
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Bloom's Taxonomy is often discussed only in terms of its cognitive domain (Remember, Understand, Apply...), but Bloom and colleagues actually proposed THREE domains of educational objectives. Besides the cognitive domain, the other two are:

options.option_text: Affective domain (attitudes, values, feelings) and Psychomotor domain (physical/motor skills)

explanation: Bloom's Taxonomy has three domains: Cognitive (thinking/knowledge), Affective (attitudes, values, emotional responses), and Psychomotor (physical movement and motor skills) — a classic, frequently-tested completeness fact.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Bloom's Taxonomy — Three Domains
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: An objective like 'the student will value cleanliness and voluntarily keep the classroom tidy' primarily targets which domain of Bloom's Taxonomy?
explanation: The affective domain concerns attitudes, values, and emotional responses (like valuing cleanliness) — distinct from the cognitive domain (knowledge/thinking) and psychomotor domain (physical skills).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch6 — Bloom's Taxonomy — Three Domains
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: An objective like 'the student will be able to correctly hold and use a pair of scissors to cut along a straight line' primarily targets which domain of Bloom's Taxonomy?
explanation: The psychomotor domain concerns physical movement and motor skill coordination (like handling scissors) — distinct from the cognitive (knowledge) and affective (attitudes/values) domains.
